To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• We present a novel method for learning face representations that can be used for face recognition, verification or clustering.

a) we propose a new method to train deep convolutional networks to directly learn a mapping from faces to a compact Euclidian embedding space b) we propose an algorithm for mining hard triplets from large datasets and c) we show that our embedding achieves state of the art performance on several tasks, including face recognition, verification, and clustering.
• A deep convolutional network can be trained to learn a representation of faces that is suitable for face recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the problem of face recognition.
the following questions: How can we learn to represent images of faces in a compact vector embedding space such that distances directly correspond to similarity?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper presents a system, called Facenet that directly learns a map from face images to compact Euclidean space, where distances directly correspondto a measure of face similarity.
FaceNet is the best method for face recognition and verification, and it has the best results for both of these tasks.
FaceNet is the best face recognition system available to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel approach to learn face embeddings and we show that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard benchmarks.
FaceNet is a deep learning approach that can learn a face embedding in a single pass.
it is the first time a deep network is trained on triplet losses and the first time a face recognition accuracy is achieved over 99% on LFW.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple yet powerful embedding learned using triplet embedding loss can be used to achieve excellent results on face verification, face recognition and clustering tasks.
it demonstrates how to learn a good representation directly on the task that one cares about.

it is possible to achieve state of theart performance using a simple yet strong embedding space, and that this representation can be learned directly from the training data without the need for expensive triplet mining.
